While developing the tragic, vulnerable character of Dominic Kearney, Barry Keoghan organically introduced one of the character’s most distinct physical traits. During production on the remote Irish islands, Keoghan randomly found a long wooden stick with a hook on the end while walking around the set. He decided that Dominic would carry it with him everywhere, using it to playfully hook things, swat at the grass, and give his hands a constant, restless physical action. Writer-director Martin McDonagh loved the spontaneous addition so much that the “Dominic stick” became a permanent fixture of his wardrobe, perfectly illustrating the character’s childlike innocence, nervous energy, and aimless wandering around the island.

The Banshees of Inisherin (2022), written and directed by Martin McDonagh, starring Colin Farrell, Brendan Gleeson, Kerry Condon, Barry Keoghan. Set on a remote island off the west coast of Ireland during the 1920s Civil War, a lifelong friendship is abruptly and inexplicably terminated by one of the men, leading to a rapidly escalating, darkly comedic, and ultimately devastating series of consequences for the entire tight-knit community.
